card.name: The word at before dosing intervals
card.fires_on: The word "at" (or a word right after it, like "two" or "approximately") in dose-adjustment instructions, just before a time interval such as "2-week intervals".

modes.label: "at" before an interval
modes.description: The word "at" follows a dose change or repeat dose and comes right before a spacing like "2 to 4 week intervals".
modes.example: the dose can be increased<< at>> 2-week intervals up to 4

modes.label: Word after "at" in the interval phrase
modes.description: A number or hedge word sits between "at" and the hyphenated unit or the word intervals.
modes.example: by 0.8 g three times per day with meals at<< two>>-week intervals as necessary to achieve target serum

card.writes: It favors hyphenated measure forms like "-minute" or "-pound" and suppresses the word "form".
card.plain: It marks the spot where a label says how often a dose can be stepped up or down, such as every 2 weeks.
